$comment: Teaching points the coverage map does not hold, because the worksheet types under them were made after it. Same fields as a coverage-map point (tp, grade, skill, code, strand). Kept few: a new type normally joins an existing point. A point marked `led` is taught by the teacher without a page (a routine with real objects, a number talk): it has no worksheet type by design.

points.skill: Plan and write a short story or message: a story map, a comic strip, a character description, a postcard
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction word problems within 100
Decode and encode a message with a key (picture code, number code, complete the key, make your own)
Say what can be measured about an object: how long, how heavy, how much it holds
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters with body benchmarks, then measure
Explain why a way of adding or subtracting works, with place value and blocks or a drawing
Read a first book made only of words the class can sound out and of taught heart words, and draw what each page says
Read a first picture book with purpose and understanding: sight words, a repeating sentence, and a picture for the new word
Say whether an outcome of drawing from a bag is certain, possible or impossible, and test a guess in an experiment with a tally and bars
Compare the chance of an outcome in two bags (more likely, less likely, the same) without fractions
Solve two-step word problems with the four operations, write the problem as one equation with a letter for the unknown, and check the answer against an estimate from rounded numbers
Ask and answer questions about key details in a short informational text and find the sentence that tells the answer
Name the main topic of an informational text and retell two or three key details that tell about it
Use headings, bold words, a caption and a glossary to find facts and word meanings in an informational text
Listen to a short fact text, read along, and answer questions about its key details with a picture
Name what a whole fact text is about and tell two key details of it
Tell which picture goes with which sentence of a fact text, and what the picture shows of it
Tell what comes first and what comes next in a fact text that tells a change
Name the main topic of an informational text of several paragraphs and what each paragraph is mostly about
Use headings, bold print, captions, a glossary, and an index to find facts in an informational text
Read a diagram with labels and arrows together with a text and tell what the diagram adds to the text
Describe the steps of a how-it-is-made text in order and tell why one step comes before another
Tell what two short fact texts on one topic both say and what only one of them says
Ask and answer questions about an informational text and show the paragraph and the sentence that prove each answer
Determine the main idea of an informational text of four paragraphs, recount the key details that support it, and tell what each paragraph is mostly about
Use the table of contents, headings, key words in bold, a sidebar, the glossary, and the index of a text to find information quickly
Describe how the events, steps, and ideas of an informational text connect, with words of time and sequence and of cause and effect
Ask and answer questions about a story and show the paragraph and the sentence that prove each answer
Retell a fable or folktale in order, determine its central message, and explain how the events of the story show it
Describe the characters of a story by their traits and feelings and explain how what they do leads to what happens next
Come to a group talk about a story prepared, and use notes and the story itself to explain ideas
Describe how a character in a story responds to a problem: what the character does and feels, and what happens because of it
Retell a fable by its beginning, middle, and end and tell the lesson it teaches
Ask and answer questions about key details in a short story and find the sentence that tells the answer
Describe the characters, the setting, and the big event of a story with key details
Retell a story by its beginning, middle, and end and tell the lesson it teaches
Find words in a story that tell how a character feels and words that appeal to the senses
Identify who is telling the story at different points: the narrator or one of the characters
Tell who a story is about, where it happens, and one big thing that happens in it
Retell a story heard aloud in order: the beginning, the middle, and the end
Answer who, where, what, and how questions about a story heard aloud, and ask a question about it
Match each part of a story heard aloud to the picture that shows it
Read and spell one-syllable words with a silent e, and tell how the e changes the vowel sound
Read and spell one-syllable words in which ai or ay spells long a
Read and spell one-syllable words in which ee or ea spells long e
Read and spell one-syllable words in which oa or ow spells long o
Read and spell one-syllable words with the digraphs ck and ng at the end and wh at the start
Read and spell one-syllable words that start with a consonant blend (s-blends, l-blends, r-blends)
Read and spell short-vowel words that end in a consonant blend (nd, mp, st, nk)
Tell naming words (nouns) from action words (verbs) and find the action word in a sentence
Find the capital letter at the start of a sentence and in the word I, and fix a sentence that starts with a small letter
Tell a telling sentence from an asking sentence and end it with a period or a question mark
Say a complete sentence about a picture and make it longer with words that tell where or when
Use a map or a diagram together with the words of a text to answer where, when, why, and how questions, and tell which source gave the answer
Use the place words in, on top of, under, next to, above, between, behind, and in front of to tell where a thing is
Hear whether the vowel sound of a one-syllable word is long or short
Tell short from long vowels in regularly spelled one-syllable words and sort the words by vowel sound
Read and spell words with the vowel teams ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, and ow and choose the team a word takes
Read and spell words with oo (moon, book), ou and ow (cloud, cow), and oi and oy (coin, boy)
Read and spell words where r changes the vowel: ar as in car and or as in fork
Read words with er, ir, and ur, which say the same sound, and check which spelling a word takes
Split and read two-syllable words that have a long vowel in one syllable (rainbow, cupcake, paper)
Read and spell common words with a part that does not follow the rules (could, would, should, because, friend)
Say the short sounds of a and i and read and spell consonant-vowel-consonant words with them (cat, map, pig, sit)
Say the short sounds of o, u, and e and read and spell consonant-vowel-consonant words with them (hot, bug, bed)
Change the first, last, or middle sound of a spoken consonant-vowel-consonant word to make a new word and spell it
Tell apart two words that differ in one letter (hat and hot, bag and big) and choose the word for a picture
Write the names of people and pets, the days of the week, and the months with a capital letter, and write a date
Choose the joining word (and, but, so, because) that fits two ideas and join two sentences into one
Use a verb to tell about yesterday, today, and tomorrow (I walked, I walk, I will walk)
Add un- or re- to a known word, say what the new word means, and choose the prefix a sentence needs
Read words with the suffixes -ful, -less, and -ly, say what the suffix adds, and choose the suffix a sentence needs
Write a contraction and the two words it stands for, and show one owner with an apostrophe and s
Read compound words and other two-part words by splitting them into two parts a first grader can read
Read and spell common irregular words (said, was, of, could) by mapping the regular sounds and remembering the tricky part
Split a two-syllable word, tell whether each syllable is closed or open, and read it with the short or the long vowel
Name silent-e, vowel-team, and consonant-le syllables in longer words and build long words from their syllables
Find the base word and the suffix of words with -able, -ment, -ness, -ful, and -less, say what the word means, and choose the word a sentence needs
Read and spell Grade 3 irregular words (enough, though, ocean, island, answer) and sort ough words by the sound ough makes
Choose the joining word (and, but, or, so, because, when, if, after, before) that fits two ideas, and join two sentences with it
Tell simple, compound, and complex sentences apart and write two short sentences as a compound and as a complex sentence
Form and choose the comparing forms of adjectives and adverbs (taller, tallest; more carefully, most carefully; better, best)
Write the possessive of one owner, of more than one owner, and of an irregular plural, and tell a possessive from a plain plural
Capitalize the first word, the last word, and every important word of a title, and keep the small words small
Sort words into categories and define a word by its category and one key attribute (a duck is a bird that swims)
Read and write words with the endings -s, -es, -ed, and -ing and find the base word in each
Use a definition, a synonym, an antonym, or an example in the sentence or the next one as a clue to the meaning of a new word
Use guide words and ABC order to find a word in a dictionary or a glossary, choose the meaning that fits, and check a spelling
Explain the job of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs, and label each word of a sentence by its job
Form and use regular plurals (boxes, babies, leaves) and irregular plurals (mice, children, sheep)
Form and use the past tense of regular verbs (jumped, hopped, carried) and of common irregular verbs (ran, brought, knew)
Make the verb agree with its subject and the pronoun agree with the noun it stands for
Connect describing words (spicy, juicy, crunchy, noisy, calm) to real things and places, and use them in sentences
Tell an adjective from an adverb and choose between them by the word it tells about (a quick dog, the dog ran quickly)
Identify the front cover, the back cover, and the title page of a book, and find the title and the author on them
Follow print from left to right and from top to bottom, with the return sweep to the next line, and page by page
Match each spoken word to one written word, and tell a written word from a single letter and from a scribble
See that words are separated by spaces in print: count the words of a sentence and leave a finger space between words
Tell an opinion from a fact, find the opinion, the reasons and the conclusion of an opinion piece, and plan an opinion piece with reasons
Connect an opinion and its reasons with linking words (because, since, therefore, for example) and draft a whole opinion piece
End an opinion piece with a concluding statement that says the opinion again in new words
With a checklist and a partner, revise an opinion piece (add a reason or an example, take out what does not belong) and edit it for capitals, end marks and commas
Find the characters, the setting, the problem and the narrator of a story beginning, and plan a story of one's own with characters, a setting, a problem, three events and an ending
Write dialogue with quotation marks, commas and end marks, and show what a character feels with an action, a thought or the way the character speaks
Use time words and phrases (first, next, after that, later that day, finally) to put the events of a story in order, and draft a story with a beginning, three events and an ending
Choose a more exact word for a tired word (said, went, nice, big, good, looked) by what the sentence tells, and revise a paragraph and sentences of one's own for word choice
Take brief notes on a source in one's own words and sort the notes under headings
Introduce a topic with a sentence that fits all the notes, group related facts under headings, and plan an informative piece
Develop a topic with facts, a definition of a hard word, and details, joined by linking words, and end with a concluding sentence
Carry out a short research project: answer a research question with notes from two sources and write a short report with an introduction, three parts, a diagram, a concluding sentence and its sources
Name the parts of an opinion piece (opinion, reasons, closing sentence), join them with because, and, also, and plan an opinion piece of one's own
Write an opinion piece with an opinion, reasons joined by linking words and a closing sentence, and revise it with a partner by adding a reason or a closing sentence
Name the five parts of a friendly letter, put a comma after the greeting and after the closing, and write a friendly letter
Capitalize the names of holidays, places and products: every important word of a holiday or place name, and the brand of a product
Name the parts of a play, a poem and a chapter book (scene, stanza, chapter) and tell how each part builds on the one before
Tell who is telling a story, what the narrator or a character thinks, and how one's own point of view differs
Tell the literal from the nonliteral meaning of words and phrases in a sentence (sayings such as lend a hand, spill the beans)
Compare and contrast the lessons, settings and plots of two stories by one author about the same characters
Compare and contrast the most important points and key details of two texts on the same topic
Plan a true story in three boxes (first, next, last) and write it with time words and an ending
Tell an opinion from its reason, and write an opinion piece that names the topic, states an opinion with because and a reason, and ends
Name a topic, write facts about it and no other, and add a closing sentence
Fix capitals and end marks in a piece, and add a detail to one's own writing after a partner's question
Find the topic sentence and the closing sentence of an informative piece, sort facts under headings, and plan a piece with a topic sentence, facts, a definition, and a closing sentence
Write an informative piece with a topic sentence, facts joined by also, another, and and, a definition, and a closing sentence that gives no new fact
Read two short books on one topic, take short notes that keep each fact true and tell which book it came from, and write one part of a class report
Plan a true story of one small moment and write it in order with time words, a thought or a feeling, and an ending
Fix capital letters and end marks in a story, put its sentences in order, and add a detail to one’s own draft after a partner’s question
